interactions.mechanism: Both raise bleeding risk; combined use needs close monitoring.
interactions.note: Review whether both are needed.

interactions.mechanism: NSAIDs raise bleeding risk, especially stomach bleeding, on top of warfarin.
interactions.note: Potential alternative for clinician review.

interactions.mechanism: Ibuprofen can blunt aspirin's antiplatelet effect and adds stomach-bleeding risk.
interactions.note: Potential alternative for clinician review.

interactions.mechanism: NSAIDs can reduce blood-pressure control and strain the kidneys.

interactions.mechanism: Both raise blood potassium; risk of dangerously high potassium.
interactions.note: Needs potassium and kidney monitoring.

interactions.mechanism: Furosemide can lower potassium, which increases digoxin toxicity risk.
interactions.note: Monitor potassium levels.

interactions.mechanism: Spironolactone can affect digoxin exposure and may complicate digoxin monitoring.
interactions.note: Monitor for digoxin toxicity and consider serum-level monitoring.

interactions.mechanism: Amlodipine raises simvastatin exposure, increasing muscle-damage risk; simvastatin dose is capped.
interactions.note: Potential alternative for clinician review.

interactions.mechanism: Omeprazole can reduce formation of clopidogrel's active metabolite and reduce antiplatelet activity.
interactions.note: Potential alternative for clinician review; verify against official prescribing information.

interactions.mechanism: NSAIDs can increase gastrointestinal and overall bleeding risk when combined with anticoagulant therapy.
interactions.note: Potential alternative for clinician review.

interactions.mechanism: NSAID/COX-2 therapy can increase bleeding risk when combined with anticoagulant therapy.

interactions.note: Monitor anticoagulation closely; clinician review required.

interactions.note: Monitor for digoxin toxicity and serum concentration.

interactions.mechanism: Esomeprazole can reduce formation of clopidogrel's active metabolite and reduce antiplatelet activity.
interactions.note: Potential alternative for clinician review; verify against official prescribing information.

interactions.mechanism: Vitamin K in leafy greens can affect warfarin response; consistent intake is important.
interactions.note: Do not make major dietary changes without clinical guidance.

interactions.mechanism: Alcohol can alter anticoagulant response and may increase bleeding risk.
interactions.note: Avoid large or sudden changes in alcohol intake; clinician review required.

interactions.mechanism: Grapefruit can increase exposure to atorvastatin and may increase adverse-effect risk.
interactions.note: Review quantity and frequency with a clinician or pharmacist.

interactions.mechanism: Grapefruit can substantially increase simvastatin exposure and increase the risk of muscle toxicity.
interactions.note: Avoidance is generally preferred; clinician review required.

interactions.mechanism: Excessive alcohol intake can increase the risk of adverse effects associated with metformin, particularly in susceptible patients.
interactions.note: Clinician review required for heavy or regular alcohol use.

interactions.mechanism: Calcium-containing foods can reduce levothyroxine absorption when taken too close together.
interactions.note: Separate administration according to clinical instructions.

interactions.mechanism: Calcium can reduce ciprofloxacin absorption when taken together.
interactions.note: Separate administration according to product instructions.

interactions.mechanism: Alcohol can add to the risk of gastrointestinal irritation and bleeding associated with aspirin.
interactions.note: Clinician review required for regular alcohol use.

interactions.mechanism: Heavy or repeated alcohol use can increase the risk of liver injury with paracetamol.
interactions.note: Dose and alcohol-use context require clinical review.

interactions.mechanism: Cranberry products have been reported to affect warfarin response in some circumstances.
interactions.note: Keep intake consistent and seek clinical advice about major dietary changes.

interactions.mechanism: Calcium can reduce levothyroxine absorption when taken too close to the medicine.
interactions.note: Separate administration according to clinical instructions.

interactions.mechanism: High dietary fiber can reduce or alter levothyroxine absorption in some patients.
interactions.note: Keep dietary patterns reasonably consistent and follow clinician instructions.
